# TigerSpool RFID

> ESP32-S3 firmware for a small touchscreen box that reads a TigerTag NFC chip on
> a filament spool and writes what it says — material, brand, colour, temperatures
> — into a 3D printer's slot. Printers are imported from the user's TigerTag
> account; nothing is typed on the device. Open source, MIT.

The box is a Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-2 (2.0" 240×320, 16 MB flash, 8 MB
octal PSRAM) with a PN532 reader on UART1. The interface is LVGL 8 over
LovyanGFX. One printer backend per brand — Bambu Lab over MQTT, Creality and
Snapmaker over WebSocket, FlashForge over HTTP — behind a single interface.

If you are an agent about to change something here, read `AGENTS.md` and
`CODEMAP.md` before touching a file, and run `bash scripts/verify.sh` before
reporting the work done. The Landmines table in `CODEMAP.md` is the highest-value
thing in this repository: nineteen behaviours that look like bugs and are not, or
look fine and are not, each of which cost somebody a debugging session.

## Working here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): repository layout, and where the rules are.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): what the board is, the index of every rule (one line each, pointing at `.agents/rules/`), the workflow commands, and a symptom-to-fix table for every guard.
- `.agents/rules/`: one file per rule, each with the rule, why it exists and how to apply it.
- [CODEMAP.md](CODEMAP.md): what each source file owns, what it must not be asked to do, and the Landmines table.
- [WORKLOG.md](WORKLOG.md): everything done since the last commit, in Keep a Changelog headings. Release notes are written from it, never from memory.
- [docs/ADOPTING-THIS-STANDARD.md](docs/ADOPTING-THIS-STANDARD.md): which parts of this way of working transferred from a sibling project, which were dropped and why, and the guards no standard predicted. Read first if you are bringing another repository up to this line.
- [docs/REVIEW-BRIEF.md](docs/REVIEW-BRIEF.md): the standing brief for a code review — read-only, six axes, and the output format.

## How it works

- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the layering, the design rules for the state machine, and why a printer backend knows nothing about the screen.
- [docs/ONBOARDING.md](docs/ONBOARDING.md): the first-boot journey — language, Wi-Fi by QR, then linking a TigerTag account.
- [docs/WIFI-PROVISIONING.md](docs/WIFI-PROVISIONING.md): the captive portal, and why there is no separate provisioning firmware.
- [docs/ACCOUNT-PAIRING.md](docs/ACCOUNT-PAIRING.md): email/password and the code-and-QR Google flow, and why RFC 8628 device flow was evaluated and rejected.
- [docs/ACCOUNT-DATA.md](docs/ACCOUNT-DATA.md): the Firestore shape a printer arrives in.
- [docs/OTA.md](docs/OTA.md): the partition layout, and the release decisions that stop being decisions after the first public release.
- [docs/PRINTER-COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/PRINTER-COMPATIBILITY.md): which printers work, what "supported" means, and the slot-naming table per brand.
- [docs/WIRING.md](docs/WIRING.md) and [hardware/pinout.md](hardware/pinout.md): the four wires. **The reader is on GPIO43/44, never GPIO6/7** — that pair is an I²C bus with pull-ups on this board, and a reader wired there answers and returns random UIDs.

## Verification

Eleven guards behind one command, `bash scripts/verify.sh`. Each names the file
and the line, each fails loudly rather than passing when its input set is empty,
and CI runs the same file rather than its own copy. They check file format,
generated files against their generators, translation tables against their enums,
every drawn string against the compiled font's real character range, that
committed text is English, that documented device names and reader wiring match
what the code builds, that drawn text comes from the translation table, and that
the version has release notes.

The device can be inspected without standing in front of it:
`http://<device>.local/screen.bmp` returns the current framebuffer and
`/api/tap?x=&y=` injects a touch, so a screen can be opened, driven and read back
from a desk.

## Not there yet

- No firmware signing. Over-the-air update works and its connection is verified against the root CA store, so the device knows who it is talking to; it does not know who produced the image. Signing is deliberately open, and worth doing only with a key that never touches CI — see `docs/OTA.md`.
- No Elegoo or Anycubic backend. Both protocols are documented; the firmware is not written.
- On-device strings carry no diacritics: the compiled font is ASCII plus degree and bullet. Restoring them needs a generated Latin subset font, and Polish needs Latin Extended-A beyond that.

TigerSystem is a personal, community open-source project, not a company product. Everything
stays free; voluntary support goes to its maintainer:
